The voltmeter is connected in parallel with the ideal cell (negligible internal resistance), so it always measures the cell's EMF, E. Thus, the new voltmeter reading is . Initially, the total resistance is R_total_0 = ( * ) / ( + ) = (2R * R) / (2R + R) = 2R/3. The initial current is = E / (2R/3) = 3E/2R. When bulb Z burns out, its branch becomes an open circuit. The new total resistance is just the resistance of the branch with bulbs X and Y, R_total_new = 2R. The new current is = E / (2R). The ratio of the new current to the old current is / = (E/2R) / (3E/2R) = 1/3. Therefore, the new ammeter reading is (1/3).
